```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
q1 = "SELECT * FROM salaries"
q2 = "SELECT * FROM collegeplaying"
df_salaries = pl.read_database(q1, con, infer_schema_length=None)
df_college = pl.read_database(q2, con, infer_schema_length=None)

byui_player_salaries = df_salaries.select(
    ["playerID", "salary", "yearID", "teamID"]
).join(
    df_college.select(["playerID", "schoolID"]).filter(pl.col("schoolID") == "idbyuid").unique(),
    on="playerID",
    how="inner",
)
byui_player_salaries
```


## QUESTION 2

__1. Pick any two baseball teams and compare them using a metric of your choice (average salary, home runs, number of wins, etc). Be creative! Write an SQL query to read in the table(s) you need, then use polars to manipulate the data. Finally, make a graph using Lets-Plot to visualize the comparison. What do you learn?__

__Find the top ten teams by number of all stars per season and then by the total team spending for that year and the top ten teams by yearly team spending and then by the allstars entries for that year__

When filtering down for the top ten teams by allstar count for a given year we find all but one of the top ten team seasons are spending in the hundreds of millions. The exception is Seattle in 2001 with 74.7 million dollars spent for 8 all stars. Four of the top ten teams sorted by allstars entries and then yearly team spend are below that one year of seattle in team entries at 7, despite spending 50-106% more.

When we flip which column we sort by first we see all ten of the top ten spending more than 200 million dollars and yet only one has eight allstars entries. All the rest have 5 at most with the majority being 3 or less. These two charts combined show a weak correlation between team spend and allstar entries where team seasons with high allstar entries generally cost 10+ million dollars across the team, but high pay alone does not guarantee you a lot of all stars.

```{python}
q3="SELECT * from allstarfull"

df_allstars = pl.read_database(q3,con, infer_schema_length=None)

df_team_salaries = df_salaries.group_by(["teamID", "yearID"]).agg(yearly_team_spend_millions=pl.col("salary").sum()/1000000)

df_allstars_teams = df_allstars.group_by([ "teamID", "yearID"]).agg(allstars_entries = pl.col("playerID").n_unique())

df_allstars_team_spend = df_allstars_teams.join(df_team_salaries, on=["teamID", "yearID"], how="left").filter(pl.col("yearly_team_spend_millions").is_not_null())

df_allstars_team_year = df_allstars_team_spend.with_columns(team_year=pl.col("teamID") + " - " + pl.col("yearID").cast(pl.String)).select("team_year","allstars_entries","yearly_team_spend_millions")

df_allstars_first = df_allstars_team_year.sort(["allstars_entries","yearly_team_spend_millions"], descending=True).head(10)

df_team_spend_first = df_allstars_team_year.sort(["yearly_team_spend_millions","allstars_entries"], descending=True).head(10)
```

```{python}

)
```

    + scale_y_continuous(breaks=list(range(200,235,5)), limits=(200,235))
)

Below is my original attempt and charts from the AI written data wrangling. I wanted to find the average team salary of the top ten teams in the hall of fame based on the proportion of votes above the required minimum for all stars access. I struggled to manipulate the data the way I wanted to be able to see the average salary spent per hall of fame entry for the top ten teams by number of entries so I had AI write up the correct logic so I could chart it and see the data. 

AI Chat: 
```{python}
q3x = "SELECT * FROM halloffame"

df_halloffame = pl.read_database(q3x, con, infer_schema_length=None)
# my original attempt at manipulating the data for the first goal
df_yearly_salaries = df_salaries.group_by(["playerID", "teamID"]).agg(
    yearly_salary=pl.col("salary").sum()
)
df_halloffame_salaries = df_halloffame.join(
    df_yearly_salaries, left_on="playerID", right_on="playerID", how="inner"
).filter(
    (pl.col("inducted") == "Y")
    & (pl.col("category") == "Player")
    & (pl.all_horizontal(["votes", "ballots", "needed", "yearly_salary"]).is_not_null())
)
df_team_halloffame = (
    df_halloffame_salaries.group_by(pl.col("teamID"))
    .agg(
        hall_of_famers=pl.col("playerID").count(),
        total_ballots=pl.col("ballots").sum(),
        total_needed=pl.col("needed").sum(),
        total_votes=pl.col("votes").sum(),
        total_yearly_salary=pl.col("yearly_salary").sum(),
    )
    .with_columns(
        average_yearly_salary=(
            pl.col("total_yearly_salary") / pl.col("hall_of_famers")
        ),
        average_votes=(pl.col("total_votes") / pl.col("hall_of_famers")),
        average_needed=(pl.col("total_needed") / pl.col("hall_of_famers")),
        average_ballots=(pl.col("total_ballots") / pl.col("hall_of_famers")),
    )
    .with_columns(
        average_vote_proportion=pl.col("average_votes") / pl.col("average_needed")
    )
    .sort(["hall_of_famers", "average_vote_proportion"], descending=True)
    .select(
        [
            "teamID",
            "hall_of_famers",
            "average_yearly_salary",
            "average_votes",
            "average_needed",
            "average_vote_proportion",
        ]
    )
    .head(10)
)
```

```{python}
# AI's code to manipulate the data that I wanted to show initially
q3 = "SELECT * FROM halloffame"

df_halloffame = pl.read_database(q3, con, infer_schema_length=None)

# Successful player induction records with voting data
df_inducted = df_halloffame.filter(
    (pl.col("inducted") == "Y") & (pl.col("category") == "Player")
).drop_nulls(["votes", "needed", "ballots"])

# Keep original salary rows for those players
df_halloffame_salaries = df_salaries.drop_nulls(["salary"]).join(
    df_inducted.select("playerID").unique(),
    on="playerID",
    how="semi",
)

# Average salary across player/team/year salary records
df_team_salaries = df_halloffame_salaries.group_by("teamID").agg(
    average_yearly_salary_millions=pl.col("salary").mean() / 1000000
)

# Each induction record appears once per team
df_team_votes = (
    df_inducted.join(
        df_halloffame_salaries.select(["playerID", "teamID"]).unique(),
        on="playerID",
        how="inner",
    )
    .group_by("teamID")
    .agg(
        hall_of_famers=pl.col("playerID").count(),
        average_votes=pl.col("votes").mean(),
        average_needed=pl.col("needed").mean(),
        average_vote_margin=(pl.col("votes") - pl.col("needed")).mean(),
    )
    .with_columns(
        average_vote_proportion=(pl.col("average_votes") / pl.col("average_needed"))
    )
)

df_team_halloffame = (
    df_team_votes.join(df_team_salaries, on="teamID", how="inner")
    .sort(
        ["hall_of_famers", "average_vote_proportion"],
        descending=True,
    )
    .head(10)
)
```

```{python}
(
    ggplot(
        df_team_halloffame,
        aes(x="teamID", y="average_yearly_salary_millions", fill="hall_of_famers"),
    )
    + geom_bar(stat="identity", position="dodge")
    + labs(
        x="Team ID",
        y="Average Yearly Salary in Millions",
        title="Average Hall of Famer Salary by Team",
        subtitle="Top 10 teams by Hall of Fame Entries",
        fill="Hall of Famers"
    )
).show()
```
